record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the Weyl-number ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing traces; the author explicitly conjectures that it should even support non-vanishing singular spectral traces.

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Show that LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing traces.
In my opinion, LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing singular spectral traces with a probability of 99 %.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space and, more generally, let X, Y be Banach spaces. For a bounded linear operator T : X → Y and an integer n ≥ 1, the n-th Weyl number is defined by
  x_n(T) = sup { a_n(T A) : A : ℓ_2 → X, ‖A‖ ≤ 1 },
where a_n(S) denotes the n-th approximation number of S, i.e. a_n(S) = inf{ ‖S − R‖ : rank R < n }. The Lorentz–Weyl operator ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} is the class of operators T (between arbitrary Banach spaces) for which
  ‖T‖_{LWEYL_{1,∞}} := sup_{n ≥ 1} n · x_n(T) < ∞.

A trace on an operator ideal I (defined on the class of all Banach spaces) is a linear functional τ : I(X,X) → ℂ for every Banach space X, satisfying the trace property τ(AB) = τ(BA) whenever the composition makes sense, and which is consistent under restriction to subspaces. The trace τ is called non-vanishing if there exists some Banach space X and some T ∈ I(X,X) with τ(T) ≠ 0. A trace is called a spectral trace if τ(T) depends only on the eigenvalue sequence of T, and singular if it vanishes on all finite-rank operators.

Problem. Decide whether the operator ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} admits a non-vanishing trace. More strongly, decide whether LWEYL_{1,∞} admits a non-vanishing singular spectral trace.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the question of whether the Lorentz–Weyl ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} supports a non-vanishing (singular spectral) trace was found. The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces, and no subsequent paper resolving it appears in available search results.

status_evidence.title: Pietsch's variants of s-numbers for multilinear operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Pietsch Weyl numbers in the context of operator ideals on Banach spaces but does not address the existence of non-vanishing traces on LWEYL_{1,∞}.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on Weyl numbers does not resolve the existence of non-vanishing traces on the Lorentz–Weyl ideal LWEYL_{1,∞}.
